findings.title: Combine refcount/double-free path is never exercised by the in-file NRT leak guard
findings.description: The module ends with an NRT alloc/free balance guard (lines 372-377: `alloc_delta != free_delta` -> WARNING + exit(1)) which is the file's only runtime check that the meminfo lifecycle (export_meminfo/borrow_structref/release_meminfo) is balanced. That guard validates only the callback paths the queries actually drive: state_size, init, update, finalize, destroy. DuckDB invokes `_irr_combine_impl` (lines 170-190) only when it merges thread-local / partitioned partial aggregate states. All three test datasets are tiny (test 1: ungrouped, 12 rows; test 2: 18 rows / 2 groups; test 3: 1 row), so DuckDB's hash aggregate runs single-threaded with a single partial per group and almost certainly never calls combine. The combine path is exactly where the focus risks (double-free across combine, source/target borrow balance, state aliasing) live, yet it carries no coverage from the guard. Per the architecture note (udaf.md sections 5/8 and risk #1/#2), the borrow net-zero property in combine depends on `removerefctpass` being disabled by an NRT-alloc symbol in the impl body (here, via `vector_extend` -> `numpy.empty`); if a numba version inlines/lowers `vector_extend` such that no NRT_MemInfo_alloc symbol lands in `_irr_combine_impl`, the surviving borrow incref (from `borrow_structref`, a separate NRT-typed @njit unit) would be paired with a stripped scope-exit decref, leaking +1 per merged source and target — silently, only under parallel aggregation, with no guard coverage.
findings.impact: A combine-specific refcount imbalance (leak, or in the mirror case an early free / use-after-free of a partial state) would ship undetected: the example asserts correctness only for paths DuckDB exercises on small single-threaded inputs, and combine is not among them. The risk is dormant until a large/parallel aggregation runs in a downstream consumer.
findings.recommendation: Force the combine path to run inside the guarded region: e.g. run one query against a table large enough (or with `SET threads` / `PRAGMA threads` raised and `force_parallelism`) to produce multiple partial states per group, then keep the existing alloc==free assertion. This turns the combine borrow/release balance and the no-aliasing property of vector_extend into a checked invariant rather than dead, unvalidated code.

notes: Reviewed examples/irr.py in full against numbox/utils/meminfo.py (export_meminfo +1 / borrow_structref net-zero / release_meminfo -1) and numbox/core/vector/vector.py (vector_push, vector_extend). The core lifecycle is sound: init's export_meminfo +1 is balanced 1:1 by destroy's release_meminfo; vector_extend (vector.py:140) COPIES src elements into a fresh/owned dst buffer, so combine creates no shared buffer and cannot double-free; the structref dtor frees the nested cashflows/periods vectors at refct 0. Handle lifetimes in register_irr are correct: the single dbl_type_p is created once, used for 4 add_parameter + set_return_type calls, then destroyed once (DuckDB copies logical types on add); the aggregate function handle is destroyed only after duckdb_register_aggregate_function (which copies the definition); tp_buf/func_buf numpy buffers are read synchronously in the same statement as their ctypes.data. No raw ctypes.from_address reads of movable Python objects exist in this file. No double-free or use-after-free of DuckDB handles found. The removerefctpass/inlining fragility (udaf.md risk #1, numbox-surface.md RISK-5) is a numbox-level concern flagged there; the one irr.py-specific consequence — that the combine path carrying that fragility is not covered by the file's own leak guard — is captured as EX-irr-MEM-1. Could not empirically measure per-callback net refcounts (no test execution permitted), so the underlying leak is rated low severity / medium confidence rather than asserted.
